name: a small garden bed seen from above: a weathered plank frame around four tilled soil ridges with bean plants climbing short stakes in rows, some empty spots
label: wasteland_ruins/crop-bed-b

surfaces.part: soil ridges with bean plants and stakes

answer.evidence: The 80x64 tile is a ground texture with a rectangular garden bed (rows 16-47) drawn from straight above. The frame is a thin 1-2 row outline. Rows 24-25, 31-32 and 38-39 show soil ridge furrows as horizontal bands, and the bean plants and stakes are scattered on top of them. There is no front face of 3 or more rows, no eave line and no vertical south face. The whole bed is a flat plate seen from above, which matches the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 5 visible tones per tile. That is above the grass reference (3) and below the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 0%, and the dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline is dark brown beside the soil and planks, not a sticker line. Even so, the whole piece uses only 16 distinct colours. The soil ramp has about 3-4 browns, the plank frame about 2-3, and the beans about 2-3 greens. That is shallower than the 5-6 steps per material in Beodeul. The soil texture is mottled with dark clods and specks, but it is repetitive and noisier than the references' per-clump and per-stone shading. The bed is small and centred, and the plank frame is thin and fairly uniform, with little per-plank grain or highlight. The bean plants are tiny and tonally simple. Next to the references it reads as a competent but slightly thinner, lower-ramp piece.
